Postposed article: γυναικῶν has already stood in front of τῶν πρώτων, so the English determiner stays on the noun and this article realizes nothing (rules 23, 31, 57). Rule 57 routes an article that follows its noun to rule 31, whose test is where the article stands and not what it governs; the earlier τῶν σεβομένων Ἑλλήνων in this same verse precedes its noun and therefore does take 'of the'. Giving this article 'of the' under rule 21 is the competing reading.

review_notes: Corrected the second genitive phrase, γυναικῶν τε τῶν πρώτων → 'and of the chief women'. The accepted alignment gave 'of the' to the postposed τῶν under rule 21, but rule 57 sends an article that follows its noun to rule 31, and rule 31 leaves the determiner on the noun, supplying one there when the noun is anarthrous. So γυναικῶν takes the discontinuous 'of the … women' headed on the noun, τῶν is unrepresented, and πρώτων keeps a bare 'chief'.

The first genitive phrase is unaffected, its article standing in front of Ἑλλήνων, so 'of the' remains there; the Greek differs in article placement, which is what licenses the two analyses side by side (rules 24, 56).
Both τε particles stay aligned because the ASV writes two English 'and's and no καί answers either of them (rule 70).
